The Value of a Human Life by Earlinwe

From the Artist's DeviantArt:

I have already been here a long time ago, when I was a young girl... My grandfather knew countless stories about this land, and one day, I pointed to him the poem that was carved at the base of the statue. The strange letters had seen hundreds of winters and monsoon rains, but they were still readable by the few people who understood that ancient language... He smiled, and started deciphering the text for me:

"Throw all your riches in the river,

Your glittering gems and tinkling necklaces,

Your sweet wines and delicate perfumes,

Your creations of mind and hand...

Throw them all in the stream,

Until you fill the riverbed, the canyon, the ocean.

Only then will you understand

The value of a human life."

I laughed. It sounded so absurd! Who would throw jewels away? They were so beautiful! Oh, I knew our ancestors, the heroic Hok'ten tribes, despised wealth, but did they disregard beauty as well? When I asked my grandfather, I didn't understand the sadness I saw in his eyes. He told me the statue had been built by the Landari, who lived here even before our ancestors. I was so excited by the venerable age of the statue that I missed the most important part.

A few years later, I finally understood. There was nobody left of the Landari people. The riverbed and canyon had already been filled with their perfumes and jewels, and their blood had dyed the sea red.
